screeningScope: Full-text source, eligibility, study-design, taxonomy, and synthesis-readiness review of the original queue positions 1-12.

decisionDefinitions.INCLUDE: Eligible for evidence extraction and synthesis after full-text review.
decisionDefinitions.DEGRADED: A required source or verification element was unavailable.

records.sourceFile: In-season monitoring of hip and groin strength, health and function in elite youth soccer- Implementing an early detection and management strategy over two consecutive seasons.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: A longitudinal cohort of 27 elite male youth soccer players used monthly adductor strength, strength-ratio, and HAGOS monitoring with predefined alerts. The system generated 105 alerts involving 70% of players, while group strength and HAGOS measures improved early in-season.
records.limitations: Single small male youth cohort without a control group; the alert system was described, not validated as an injury-prediction rule.
records.synthesisCaution: Use as an implementation and monitoring example, not proof that the stated thresholds prevent injury.

records.sourceFile: Chronic cannabis consumption and physical exercise performance in healthy adults - A systematic review.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: Four eligible studies found no consistent difference in VO2max or physical work capacity between chronic cannabis users and non-users; only one study found a resting-heart-rate difference.
records.limitations: Only four cross-sectional studies, several with small samples and older low-potency cannabis exposure; causality cannot be established and recovery or endurance outcomes were not assessed.
records.synthesisCaution: Absence of detected performance effects is not evidence of safety, recovery benefit, or no impairment under current products and doses.

records.sourceFile: Acute-chronic workload ratio and training monotony variations over the season in professional soccer - A systematic review.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: The review included 27 professional-soccer studies and documented wide seasonal ranges and methodological variation in acute:chronic workload ratio and training monotony measures.
records.limitations: Substantial heterogeneity in designs, workload definitions, measures, durations, and injury outcomes; the reviewed data did not conclusively distinguish injured from non-injured players.
records.synthesisCaution: Do not promote universal ACWR risk thresholds or causal injury claims; emphasize descriptive monitoring and method standardization.

records.sourceFile: Do environmental tempeatures and altitudes affect physical outputs of elite soccer athletes in match conditions - A systematic review of the 'real world' studies.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: Twelve real-world studies indicated that temperature and altitude can impair selected elite-football match outputs, but the direction and magnitude of effects were inconsistent.
records.limitations: Small evidence base with varied tracking technologies, exposure definitions, outcomes, reporting, and uncontrolled match-context confounding.
records.synthesisCaution: Frame environmental conditions as context-dependent planning inputs rather than deterministic performance penalties.

records.sourceFile: Return to play and performance after patellar fracture in American professional sports - A case-control cohort analysis.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: Across 41 professional athletes with patellar fracture, 29 returned to play (71%) after an average 217 days. Playing volume fell in year one and returned toward baseline in year two; operative cases recovered performance by year two in this cohort.
records.limitations: Retrospective public-record identification, small multi-league sample, incomparable sport metrics, and unavailable fracture characteristics and operative reports.
records.synthesisCaution: Do not infer treatment superiority or individual prognosis from the observed operative/nonoperative patterns.

records.sourceFile: Evening smartphone exposure impairs sleep quality and next-day performance in elite soccer players - A randomized controlled trial.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: In a randomized crossover trial, 16 elite male soccer players completed five nights of two-hour pre-bed smartphone use versus magazine reading. Smartphone exposure worsened sleep duration, latency, efficiency, sleepiness, and selected next-day cognitive and physical outcomes.
records.limitations: Very small, short-duration, male soccer sample; blinding was impractical and unusually large reported effects require independent replication.
records.synthesisCaution: Support pragmatic evening-device management, but avoid universal cutoffs or claims across sports, sexes, ages, and competition contexts.

records.sourceFile: Professional football (soccer) training and recovery - A longitudinal study on the effects of weekly conditioning session and workload variables.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: Twenty-four professional players were assessed at two seasonal time points. Higher chronic load was associated with a less favorable salivary testosterone/cortisol profile, while acute load showed less relationship to the selected recovery markers.
records.limitations: Single-club cohort, roster attrition, only two sampling microcycles, correlational analysis, salivary-hormone variability, and limitations of acute:chronic ratio descriptors.
records.synthesisCaution: Treat hormonal measures as contextual monitoring signals, not standalone readiness diagnoses or causal workload effects.

records.sourceFile: Combining evidence and practice to optimize neck training aimed at reducing head acceleration events in sport - A systematic review and Delphi-consensus study.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: A systematic review of 21 heterogeneous neck-training studies was combined with a three-round Delphi process involving 18 international experts, producing 57 implementation statements across five categories.
records.limitations: No quantitative synthesis was possible; intervention and assessment heterogeneity prevents firm efficacy estimates, and Delphi consensus is expert agreement rather than causal evidence.
records.synthesisCaution: Use the statements as an implementation framework while clearly separating consensus from proven reduction in head acceleration or injury.

records.sourceFile: A little pepper-upper - Systematic review of randomized controlled studies on capsaicinoids, capsinoids, and exercise performance.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: Nineteen randomized placebo-controlled trials were included; ten reported positive performance effects, with the signal appearing more often in resistance exercise than endurance exercise.
records.limitations: No meta-analysis, heterogeneous compounds, doses, outcomes, and exercise modes; adverse effects were often unreported and long-term effects remain unknown.
records.synthesisCaution: Do not convert mixed study counts into a supplement recommendation; dose, safety, and sport-specific benefit remain unresolved.

records.sourceFile: Effects of low-level laser therapy on muscular performance and soreness recovery in athletes - A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: A meta-analysis of 24 randomized or crossover studies reported improvements in selected lower-limb strength follow-ups and some recovery outcomes after low-level laser therapy.
records.limitations: Treatment parameters, muscles, timing, outcomes, and trial quality varied; the authors state that a definite therapeutic effect remains unestablished and larger robust trials are needed.
records.synthesisCaution: Present as promising but protocol-dependent evidence, not a standard recovery recommendation.

records.sourceFile: Impact of melatonin supplementation on sports performance and circulating biomarkers in highly trained athletes - A systematic review of randomized controlled trials.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: Twenty-one controlled trials using 5-100 mg melatonin were reviewed. Findings suggest improvements in selected oxidative-stress, inflammatory, and muscle-damage biomarkers, while a direct performance-enhancing mechanism or effect remains undetermined.
records.limitations: Large heterogeneity in dose, timing, exercise protocols, biomarkers, and samples; biomarker changes do not establish meaningful performance benefit.
records.synthesisCaution: Keep recovery-biomarker findings separate from direct performance claims and from individualized sleep or supplementation guidance.

records.sourceFile: Does longer-muscle length resistance training cause greater longitudinal growth in humans - A systematic review.pdf
records.evidenceSummary: Eight resistance-training studies totaling 120 participants generally favored longer-muscle-length training for muscle size and fascicle-length change, but results were mixed.
records.limitations: No study directly estimated serial sarcomere number; all but one used questionable linear-extrapolation methods for fascicle length, leaving the structural mechanism undetermined.
records.synthesisCaution: Support a cautious hypertrophy inference, not a confirmed sarcomerogenesis mechanism.
